nodes.question: What does this diff change?
nodes.note: Collapses the tree's N1-N4. A reviewer classifies the shape of a change once; the tree asks it as four yes/no questions in sequence.

edges.answer: a gate this diff itself wires, over every changed path

nodes.question: What was that ancestor gate's evaluated state at the merge date?
nodes.note: Three answers, which is the natural shape of the question and the reason this node exists. The tree splits it into N7 (is it readable) and N8 (does it withhold); a reviewer asks once and gets one of three.

edges.answer: unreadable — cannot be determined at the merge date
withholding the change from all real users
exposing the change to some real users

nodes.question: Is there an existing key that could cover this change?
nodes.note: One question; the four predicates are how it is answered, not four separate steps. ONE candidate qualifies only if it exists at merge_base, still withholds its feature from someone, is the key of the feature this change belongs to, and its off arm would cover the whole change -- the same key for all four. With none, a change whose enclosing gate still holds it back in main production (P6, P33; reached only past W3's exposing answer) is weighed for the policy's exception (W4M) rather than sent to the battery.

edges.answer: yes — one key exists at merge_base, still withholds its feature, is this change's feature, and its off arm covers the change
no usable candidate, but the enclosing gate still holds the change back from some real users in main production
no usable candidate

nodes.question: Does the PR say this part is released on its own schedule, apart from the enclosing gate's feature?

edges.answer: yes — a separate schedule or audience is stated
no stated separation: the gate still holds it back in main production

nodes.question: Is this a separate release from that key's feature?

edges.answer: yes — a separate schedule or audience is stated
no stated separation, and an ancestor gate already encloses every changed path: nothing to wire (ruling R1)
no stated separation

nodes.question: Which release-control signal does this change carry?
nodes.note: The largest collapse: five binary nodes (N15, N18-N20, N27) become one question with six answers. This is the step the binary form reads worst -- a reviewer asks "which of these applies?" once, and the tree makes them answer "is it this one?" five times.

edges.answer: a new user-reachable surface
an announcement surface shown unprompted
a change to a published interface's contract
a default, initial-state or ordering change
new per-request work on a path all customers' traffic runs through
a concrete risk on a path customers already use (the risk search)
none of these

nodes.question: Does the contract change only the outcome of what already fails or is mishandled?
nodes.note: A repair changes a contract's answer by definition: the wrong answer a client got at merge_base. P23 asks whether that is all it changes.

edges.answer: yes -- only what already fails or is mishandled changes
no -- the signal stands

nodes.question: Does the risk the search found sit only on what already fails or is mishandled?
nodes.note: A verified risk names a changed outcome on a live path; a repair's changed outcome is the wrong one being put right. P23 asks whether every changed outcome is.

edges.answer: yes -- only what already fails or is mishandled changes
no -- the signal stands
